title: MMO server and retro reconstruction discovery
summary: Review 26 pinned repositories: add 23 projects and record three deferrals.
notes: Root personally searched 29 repository queries across C64, ZX Spectrum, Amiga, Atari ST, CPC, DOS/Windows and defunct MMO reconstructions. Screened 1135 unique repository URLs against current main. Reviewed 26 available pinned trees and primary documentation/source/build files; four additional candidates could not be read and were not promoted. Requested Dungeon Runners and Tabula Rasa both have substantive server source. MMO protocol emulation is distinguished from CPU emulation and from reconstructed clients; no retail completeness inferred from login or README feature lists. No candidate programs, installers or game clients executed. Larger files are linked and selectively inspected; exact small UTF-8 proof bodies are sealed. No worker, branch or PR used.

sources.reason: Game-specific authentication, networking, dungeon/quest and combat source exists, including deterministic entity ordering, player attacks, monster perception and damage. Not merely a launcher or announcement. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

Authentication and game services, combat logout and extensive mission reconstruction. Wilderness documentation distinguishes native identities from reconstructed missing server facts and explicitly defers instance dependencies. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

Rasa.NET-derived server with an explicit final-live preservation target, client-artifact research and detailed retail-accuracy work log. D16.5 evidence is distinguished from unproven final server configuration; functionality alone is not fidelity. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

Older C++ implementation with socket queue/login, TabulaCrypt handshake, map-bound missile and actor combat structures. Partial server reconstruction, not a full-game recovery claim. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

Historical Google Code export containing authentication, game-service and JHLIB interoperability projects. Combat manager methods are empty in the inspected source, so this is partial protocol/server recovery rather than a restored playable MMO. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

From-scratch server with login/gateway services and substantive persistent quest manager, objectives and rewards, plus packet and entity systems. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

Client-reversed protocol and game server with combat and quest handlers, login/world/zone services and content reconstruction. Some archived quests are simplified deliveries and some spawns use invented placeholder camps; not faithful full-content preservation. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

From-scratch server with world objects, creature combat, networking and data loading. Latest-client interoperability and database-driven world restoration, not original server source release. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

GDL/GDLE-based reconstruction targeting February 2005 Infiltration, before Throne of Destiny. Typed combat formulas and attack-event source support the distinct historical ruleset scope. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

WildStar build 16042 server with native semantic damage calculation, quest state and objective persistence. Inspected combat and quest code retains TODOs; broad function coverage is not full retail parity. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

Elixir/OTP port of NexusForever with protocol, authentication, world and database services. Quest query/persistence source is substantive, but README warns much advertised functionality is incomplete or broken; includes custom Mythic+ features. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

Matrix Online protocol/server implementation with authentication, game services, player-object handlers and reverse-engineering proxy tools. No complete mission or combat restoration inferred. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

C# Matrix Online server with protocol parsing, combat formulas and RPC handlers. README explicitly marks missions, multiplayer, inventory and combat partial/unstable; vendors have incomplete money handling. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

Reconstructed server with semantic combat and game systems. README labels 1.52.0.1700 full support, with 1.48.0.1712 and 1.53.0.203 preliminary; these are upstream support levels rather than independently proven parity. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.

Separate server for client 1.10.0.643, optionally 1.10.0.69. README reports world exploration, powers and limited multiplayer but most combat does not work; missing packet captures and legacy behavior-tree differences remain. Reconstructed server behavior for the original client, not a reconstructed client or CPU emulator.
Parses game.pki/game.pkg archives for Dungeon Runners clients v118 and v666, with asset viewing/extraction for textures, fonts, audio and data. Not a game server.
Game-specific archive/index parsers and extraction into a dump folder from game.pkg/game.pki.
GLM packed-file and chunk-format parsing plus model conversion/viewer for Tabula Rasa. Model code also distinguishes Auto Assault LODLevel naming, but full Auto Assault support is not inferred.

Reverse-engineered UE2.5/Vanguard terrain, meshes, animation, audio and SGO prefab formats. Inspected typed SGO parser and extraction package; outputs support the separate Eternal Sagas client project.
Reconstructs DOS DrugLord v2.01 in C with an attributed byte-identical 74286-byte claim, and implements native Go game rules/events for Windows/WebAssembly.
Unofficial reconstruction of UNISOUND.COM v0.82a ISA PnP audio-card initialization utility, with named recovered functions and subsequent fixes/new card support.
Twelve-board Jumpman Junior reconstruction from frame-by-frame C64 footage: layouts, bombs, disappearing girders and measured movement. Native JavaScript world/rules and level data.
Native shared C game core recreates EGA Trek on vintage platforms, including plain C64, Amiga and Atari ST/STE; per-platform graphics, sound, storage and overlay layers.

Minimal SDL/ImGui launcher that locates tabula_rasa.exe and starts/configures the existing client. Useful adjacent utility, but inspected entry point does not establish recovered game/server logic or asset format analysis; defer launcher-only addition.

Unity Battle Squadron-labelled project has native fighter movement, shooting and an audio component, but inherited Space Shooter Tutorial material and sparse README do not establish title-specific level/rule fidelity. Defer deeper reconstruction evidence rather than present generic shooter scripts as recovered Battle Squadron.

Unity school-project 3D reinterpretation with helicopter movement and authored enemy waves. The relationship to a specific Amiga version and recovered original rules is not established; outside this focused reversing/reconstruction pass.
